Consult Summary:
- Assessment of acute, worsening lower abdominal pain with light vaginal bleeding/discharge; plan for in-person abdominal examination and pregnancy testing to clarify etiology.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe lower abdominal pain, constant and worsened over several days; pain rated ~8/10.
- Associated symptoms: Light vaginal bleeding (pink) and mild vaginal discharge; nausea without vomiting; history of constipation last week (now resolved); regular bowel movements this week.
- Onset/duration/progression: Pain began several days ago; gradually increasing in intensity and staying constant.
- Gynecologic/ obstetric history: Regular sexual activity; using Implanon (implant) for contraception; last period reported as 2–3 weeks ago or around two weeks ago; period described as light and pink (irregular menses on Implanon); last menstrual period earlier unspecified; past pregnancies: none.
- Menstrual/contraception details: Implanon in place for about a year; periods described as irregular on Implanon; last period reportedly stopped about two weeks ago with light pink discharge.
- Pregnancy status: Prior pregnancy test about one month ago; today’s plan includes a pregnancy test.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin allergy.
- Medications: No medications documented.
- Social history: Occupation – school teacher; lives with husband and husband’s family; recent travel abroad (past year); alcohol use reported as regular; smoking status not clearly documented.
- Review of systems: No fever reported; no shortness of breath or chest pain; no abdominal tenderness other than current pain described; no urinary symptoms beyond possible discharge; no weight loss clearly documented.
- Noted inconsistencies: Several conflicting statements regarding last period timing and menstrual status; irregular menses on Implanon complicates interpretation.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not provided.
- Examination findings: Not performed in this encounter; planned to be done during in-person abdominal exam.

Impression:
- Working impression: Acute lower abdominal pain with associated light vaginal bleeding/discharge; etiology unclear pending physical and pregnancy testing.

Plan:
- Arrange in-person, face-to-face abdominal examination in clinic for further assessment.
- Perform pregnancy test today; if positive, urgent review indicated.
- If symptoms worsen or inability to tolerate oral intake/fluids occurs, seek urgent evaluation before scheduled appointment.
- Schedule/coordinate appointment via support line.
- Provide guidance and follow-up contingent on exam results.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Med reconciliation: no current meds listed beyond Implanon; no daily meds documented.
  - Current vitals and physical exam findings: not available.
  - Clear obstetric history (prior pregnancies, outcomes) beyond “no pregnancies.”
  - Complete assessment of allergies (only amoxicillin noted) and any other drug intolerances.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Conflicting statements about last menstrual period (2–3 weeks ago vs “stopped” 2 weeks ago) and irregular menses on Implanon.
- Transcript quality:
  - Some unclear or garbled phrases; patient had difficulty hearing at times; not all details are fully reconciled.
